name: sar-logic-timing-gates-bad
description: Single-loop gate-level replay of the `bad` (70 ns comparator-to-latch delay -- DELIBERATELY past the 62.5 ns bit cycle) NEGATIVE-CONTROL loop of sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ -- the SAME gate-level timing-margin negative control (README.md#target-specification, issue #11's synchronous-SAR timing-margin verification, DR-0008, spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2), against the SYNTHESIZED gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist (design/sar-logic/flow/sar_ctrl/netlist/sar_ctrl.mcu7t5v0.synth.v, issue #272), split out of the original five-loop deck by issue #311 -- see sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/testbench/tb.json's evidence notes for the full decomposition rationale (identical for every one of the five split experiments) and sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ for the still-committed, unmodified five-loop deck kept for the nominal-PVT cross-check.
claim: NEGATIVE CONTROL for spec/prior-art-survey.md Sec 4.2's per-cycle timing budget, re-checked on the real synthesized gate netlist: a decision arriving after the 62.5 ns cycle's latching edge MUST corrupt the conversion. Alone (in this split experiment) it does not itself cross-check that `ok`/`lt`/`xl` pass for the right reason -- that cross-check needs all four sharing one run, which the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck still exists to provide at nominal PVT (issue #311) -- but it still independently proves this exact testbench methodology, on this DUT, at whatever corner it is run, is capable of detecting a broken conversion.
netlist_provenance: schematic (gate-level, single-loop `bad`: klt-synthesized gf180mcu_fd_sc_mcu7t5v0 netlist wrapping sar_ctrl.v, issue #272 -- not yet placed-and-routed; DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c) own P&R/STA; split from the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck by issue #311's per-loop decomposition)
analyses: meas tran aerr_bad MAX v(bad_aerr) FROM=0.1u

abs_err_delay_70ns.description: NEGATIVE CONTROL -- UNCHANGED bound, carried over from the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck (issue #311). 70 ns exceeds the 62.5 ns bit cycle; the conversion MUST come out wrong, on the real gate netlist exactly as on the ideal one.

notes: ISSUE #311 PER-LOOP DECOMPOSITION: this experiment is one of five (`sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/-lt/-xl/-bad/-tie`) split out of the single five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck. The measurement definitions, bounds and 8.5 us duration are UNCHANGED; only how many loops share one ngspice deck changed. Rationale, the cost measurement that motivated it, and the 'five slugs vs one deck-variant axis' decision are in sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/investigations/20260917-issue-303-five-loop-composition-cost.md and design/sar-logic/flow/gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's own module docstring ('Per-loop timing decomposition (issue #311)').

WHY THIS EXPERIMENT STILL MATTERS SPLIT OUT ALONE: `bad` is the family's negative control -- 'a testbench with no case that must fail is not evidence it can detect a broken conversion'. That reasoning depends on `bad` sharing a run with `ok`/`lt`/`xl` (which the five-loop sim/sar-logic-timing-gates/ deck still provides at nominal PVT for exactly this reason); this split experiment's OWN 45-point grid is instead evidence that the negative control keeps failing correctly (min 0.9 LSB error) across the full PVT range, not just at the one corner the five-loop deck can afford.

COMPUTATIONAL COST: not independently measured for this loop's own delayed-comparator-plus-T-line composition (`cmp_delay=70n`); it is structurally the same closed loop as `ok` (same controller/CDAC size, same 8.5 us duration, one loop per deck) plus a matched-50-ohm transmission line, so it is expected to cost about the same order as `ok`'s measured ~132 core-s per point (sim/sar-logic-timing-gates-ok/testbench/tb.json). A run's own record states the actual measured per-point cost.

The behavioural CDAC/comparator model and start-pulse seeding (design/sar-logic/rtl/README.md's 'Real hardware note') are UNCHANGED from the five-loop deck -- only the loop composition changed. Issue #296's comparator-output-slew fix does NOT apply to this loop: `bad`'s comparator drives a matched 50 ohm terminated transmission line, not a bare gate input, so it was never subject to the zero-time-step abort #296 fixed (see design/sar-logic/flow/gen_sar_ctrl_gates_tb.py's 'Comparator output slew' section).

What this record does NOT claim: no place-and-route, no STA/timing closure (DR-0023 follow-ons (b)/(c), issues #274/#275) -- this is a pre-layout gate-level netlist wrapped directly in SPICE, with no extracted parasitics and no real interconnect delay. It is also not evidence about real CDAC settling or comparator behaviour.
